_comment: Content-change dates for the 8 hand-authored static pages, used as <lastmod> in sitemap.xml.
REQUIREMENT: when you edit one of these pages, bump its date here in the same commit.
If you forget, that URL's lastmod goes stale (fake staleness) until someone notices.
Why a manifest rather than git commit dates: GitHub Actions checkout defaults to
fetch-depth: 1, a shallow clone, under which `git log -1 -- <file>` returns the single
fetched commit for EVERY file. That would stamp all 8 pages with the CI build date - the
exact mtime defect this change exists to remove - and it would be invisible locally where
full history is present. A stale entry on one low-churn legal page is a smaller and more
visible failure than all 8 silently collapsing on every CI run.
Dates are YYYY-MM-DD and must reflect genuine content change, never a build or deploy.
